title: Applied ML Regression Triage and Eval Harness Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the detection, triage, and mitigation process for applied-ML regressions observed by our eval harness, production telemetry, or customer reports. It covers how to use the eval-harness to reproduce failures, vet prompt sets and benchmarks, validate model onboarding and quantization profiles, and escalate to engineering or product when necessary.

Scope:
- Applies to regressions in model quality (semantic correctness, hallucination increase), metric drift on prompt sets/benchmarks, and quantization-induced quality degradation for models served by Redwood.
- Includes regressions detected in CI evals, nightly benchmark sweeps, canary traffic, and production telemetry tied to eval sentinel prompts.
- Excludes unrelated infra outages (see eng-sre runbooks) and data-pipeline bugs outside model-serving inputs.

Ownership and Roles:
- Primary owner: Applied ML (owner_team: engineering)
- On-call contacts:
  1) Aisha Patel (Applied ML) — primary triage
  2) Miguel Torres (Eval Engineer) — eval harness & reproduction
  3) Ravi Kapoor (Serving Runtime) — inference/quantization investigation
- Escalation: Product lead (e.g., Emily Chen) for customer-impacting regressions requiring rollbacks or model policy changes.

Preconditions and Signals (detection):
- Automated signals that SHOULD trigger this playbook:
  - CI Eval regressed: any nightly eval run where the primary quality score drops > 4% absolute vs baseline on core prompt set.
  - Canary drift: production canary route shows > 10% increase in semantic-error rate or > 50% increase in hallucination alerts (as computed by guardrail classifier).
  - Embedding drift: mean cosine similarity to baseline < 0.90 across benchmark queries or downstream ranking MRR drop > 5%.
  - Model-card mismatch: post-deploy guardrails flag > 5% of examples outside allowed behavior profile.
- Observability sources: eval-harness reports, Redwood Console per-route quality dashboard, SLO alerting (applied-ml-quality-slo), customer issues tagged via support.

Triage Steps (ordered):
1) Acknowledge and classify
   - Record incident: create confluence incident page and Slack thread in #applied-ml-alerts.
   - Classify severity:
     - Sev-1: Immediate customer impact (p50 regressions causing wrong billing decisions, safety failures).
     - Sev-2: Significant regression on core benchmarks or canary but mitigatable via config.
     - Sev-3: Minor drift, requires monitoring and scheduled investigation.
2) Gather evidence (collect artifacts)
   - Eval-harness run ID, commit SHA, model-version/model-variant (e.g., open-llama-13b-quant-v2), quantization profile used (e.g., qp-int8-symmetric), prompt-set and benchmark IDs.
   - Telemetry samples: 100 failing examples from canary/prod, top-k logs with token-level scores and guardrail classifier outputs.
   - Performance metrics: latency p50/p95, GPU memory footprint, KV cache hit rates.
3) Reproduce locally using eval-harness
   - Checkout the eval harness: git clone git@repo:redwood/eval-harness.git && git checkout <commit-sha>.
   - Re-run the failing benchmark: redwood-eval-runner run --suite <benchmark-id> --model <model-uri> --quant-profile <profile> --out artifacts/<run-id>.json
   - Use --replay-orig-requests to ensure identical inputs when investigating production samples.
4) Binary search changes
   - If regression appeared after a change-range, perform bisection on commits between Good SHA and Bad SHA to isolate the code or model change.
   - Test permutations: (a) model version change only, (b) quantization profile change only, (c) runtime kernel change only.
5) Validate prompt sets and benchmarks
   - Check that prompt-set preconditions hold (tokenization, deterministic seeding, context window lengths).
   - Verify that benchmark metrics are computed with the correct scoring function; rerun with label-aware scorer and/or human-in-the-loop checks for a sampled subset (N=50).
6) Quantization checks
   - Re-evaluate model without quantization (float fallback) and compare delta. If delta > 3% on quality metric for core prompts, categorize as quantization-induced.
   - Run quant-profiles test matrix: qp-int8, qp-int8-hybrid, qp-4bit, qp-4bit-gptq. Record per-profile degradation numbers.
7) Mitigation and rollback
   - For customer-impacting regressions, immediately switch canary routing to previous model-variant and/or revert runtime change. Use the Redwood Console rollback button or: redwood-admin models promote --from <prev-model> --route <route>.
   - For quantization regressions, temporarily fall back to a higher-fidelity profile (e.g., qp-int8-hybrid -> fp16) and incrementally re-test.
8) Post-triage actions
   - Create a remediation ticket with root cause hypothesis, reproducer, and fix owner.
   - Schedule a postmortem if Sev-1/Sev-2. Include regression test additions to eval harness and required guardrail improvements.

Diagnosis Checklist (quick items to run immediately):
- Does the regression reproduce with eval-harness on the exact model URI and quant profile?
- Did model weights change (new model ID) or did runtime/serving infra change?
- Did tokenization change (BPE/vocab)? Check tokenizer hashes.
- Is there an input distribution shift? Compare input token lengths and top tokens vs baseline.
- Were recent changes made to prompt templates or post-processing functions?

Repro example (commands):
- Clone harness and run suite:
  git clone git@repo:redwood/eval-harness.git && cd eval-harness
  git checkout <sha>
  make setup-env
  redwood-eval-runner run --suite core-regression-set --model open-llama-13b:2026-02-01 --quant-profile qp-int8 --out /tmp/run.json
- Re-run a single failing example with deterministic seed:
  redwood-eval-runner replay --input /tmp/sample-42.json --model open-llama-13b:2026-02-01 --seed 42 --out /tmp/replay.json

Prompt sets & benchmark vetting:
- For each failing sample, ensure the prompt set includes: canonical prompt text, golden label(s), metadata (intent, sensitivity tags), expected scoring function, and example difficulty label.
- Benchmarks must include a baseline reference score and pass/fail thresholds. Example table:
  | benchmark_id | description | baseline_score | fail_threshold | owner |
  | core-regression-set | Core production prompt set used for nightly evals | 0.82 | 0.78 | Applied ML |

Model onboarding and release checklist (quick):
- Confirm model-card fields (architecture, tokenizer_hash, expected FLOPS, quantization profiles supported).
- Run model-throughput and perf-suite: throughput p95 >= 90% of previous variant for same batch/seq distribution.
- Run full eval-harness suites (smoke + core) and human review of N=200 examples across intents.
- If quantized, validate against quant-profiles matrix and record per-profile deltas.

Quantization profile validation matrix (example):
  | profile | expected-peak-mem | expected-latency-p95 | expected-quality-delta | recommended-use |
  | qp-int8 | 42 GB | +5% | delta <= 2% | Dedicated low-cost clusters |
  | qp-int8-hybrid | 36 GB | +3% | delta <= 1% | Production default for medium models |
  | qp-4bit-gptq | 18 GB | -10% throughput | delta <= 3% | Experimental / latency-sensitive |

Quality guardrails and automated tests:
- Guardrails used in pipelines: hallucination-detector-v2, toxicity-filter, factuality-checker, sensitive-entity-detector.
- Add a targeted sentinel prompt to the core-regression-set for any new model variant that exercises edge-case behavior.
- Define automatic action for regression severity:
  - auto-shelve: if eval-harness core score drops >= 6% -> block promotion to production.
  - auto-alert: if canary guardrail triggers on > 5% of samples -> page applied-ml oncall.

Communication and SLAs:
- For Sev-1 incidents, notify customers in impacted tiers within 1 hour via support channel and provide mitigation ETA.
- For Sev-2, notify stakeholders within 8 business hours with next steps.

Postmortem and corrective actions:
- Postmortem should include: timeline, root cause, detection gaps, corrective work (tests, alert tuning, docs), owners, and verification steps.
- Add a regression test to the eval-harness (new suite + golden reference) before re-promoting the model.
- If caused by quantization, update quant-profiles registry with observed deltas and recommended minimum profile for that model family.

Runbook snippets and useful links:
- Eval harness repo: git@repo:redwood/eval-harness.git
- Eval job runner: redwood-eval-runner CLI docs: /internal/docs/redwood-eval-runner
- Model catalog: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/model-catalog
- Quant-profiles registry: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quant-profiles-index

Appendix A: Example incident timeline (short)
1) 03:02 — Nightly eval job failed (core-regression-set score dropped 5.8%).
2) 03:05 — Pager to applied-ml oncall; Slack thread opened.
3) 03:20 — Eval engineer reproduced locally; isolated quant profile change.
4) 03:45 — Rolled back canary to fp16 profile; canary quality returned to baseline.
5) 08:00 — Postmortem created; remediation ticket filed to improve preflight quantization checks.

Appendix B: Contact list
- Applied ML oncall (primary): aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Eval harness owner: miguel.torres@redwood.ai
- Serving runtime lead: ravi.kapoor@redwood.ai

Notes and conventions:
- All commands and artifacts should include the run ID and commit SHA.
- When in doubt, prioritize reproducible artifacts over heuristics; archive failing examples to the evidence bucket: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/<run-id>/

This playbook is intended to be a living document: update the quant-profiles table and benchmark thresholds as we onboard new models or update guardrail classifiers.
